subject: Re: Redwood vs Hyperscaler AB-test — latency & throughput follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@globex.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Redwood x Globex — next steps + AB test plan

Thanks again for the call today, Alex — great to meet the Globex AI team. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Summary from call:
- Primary goal: confirm perf delta (latency p95/p99 and tokens/sec) between your current hyperscaler setup and Redwood Dedicated inference.
- Workload: customer-facing summarization pipeline (max seq len ~1024, typical prompt+response ~600 tokens).
- Success criteria: p95 improvement >= 20% and tokens/sec uplift that improves cost per inference.

Proposed AB-test plan (what Redwood will run):
1) Baseline: run your representative test suite against the hyperscaler endpoint you supplied (we'll use the exact payloads you send us).
2) Redwood run: same payloads against Redwood Dedicated (same model family, quantization profile as discussed).
3) Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, memory/KV cache hit rates, and cost estimates.
4) Time windows: small smoke run (1k requests) + steady-state run (10k requests) during a 3-hour window to capture variance.

What we need from Globex to kick off:
- Confirmation of the exact endpoint + auth (or sample traces) you want tested.
- A 10k-request sample workload (CSV or JSONL).
- Any IP allowlist or VPC peering details if you want tests from your VPC.

If that looks right I'll schedule the smoke run for Thursday and the steady-state run early next week. I'll attach the test configuration doc and a template for the workload.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
[Attachment: test_configurations.md]

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. That plan looks good. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We'll provide the 10k-request JSONL (anonymized) by EOD today. Expect three payload types: short prompts (FAQ), mid-length (summaries ~400 tokens), and long (full-document condense ~1k tokens).
- Baseline numbers (our hyperscaler): p95 ~380ms, p99 ~890ms, tokens/sec ~1100 on our production-sized burst instances. Those are running a slightly different quant profile (fp16) so we'd like to see both parity and cost projections.
- We prefer Redwood to run tests from your hosted infra (no VPC peering initially) — please confirm IP ranges for allowlist so our security can open the firewall for the smoke window.

Two asks from me: 
1) Can you include CPU/GPU utilization traces and KV cache hit-rate in the results? Those are important for our infra folks.
2) Can you run one of the steady-state runs using a lower batch size (+ higher concurrency) so we capture p99 tail under concurrency stress?

If you need anything else from the Globex side I'll loop in procurement (later for contract). Looking forward to the smoke run.

—Alex
Alex Johnson

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 11:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood vs Hyperscaler AB-test — preliminary results + next steps

Alex — thanks for sending the workload sample and the baseline numbers. We completed the smoke + steady-state runs and attached the raw CSV + plots. High-level summary below (see attachments for full metrics and configs):

Key results (steady-state, model-family matched):
- p50: Redwood 58ms vs Hyperscaler 92ms
- p95: Redwood 220ms vs Hyperscaler 380ms (≈42% improvement)
- p99: Redwood 420ms vs Hyperscaler 890ms (≈53% improvement)
- Tokens/sec (sustained): Redwood 1,600 t/s vs Hyperscaler 1,100 t/s
- KV cache hit-rate (same prefix profiles): Redwood 87% vs Hyperscaler N/A (we observed higher cache efficiency due to our prefix caching path)

Notes & caveats:
- We matched model family and quantization to the closest available settings; small differences remain in kernel selection that can affect tail latency.
- The lower p99 on Redwood is driven by our optimized batching + kernel selection under high concurrency; we included a low-batch/high-concurrency run as you requested (see test_configurations.md).
- Cost modeling (rough): with observed tokens/sec, Redwood estimates a ~18–25% lower cost per 1M tokens under your workload assumptions. We can refine with your actual commit profile.

Attachments included: redwood_vs_hyperscaler_abtest_results.csv (raw lines), p95_p99_latency_plots.pdf (plots), test_configurations.md (how we ran the tests + batch/concurrency matrix).

Next steps I propose:
- 30-min sync next week to walk through the CSV & plots with your infra team (I can bring our infra engineer Logan).
- If the perf and cost look good, we can prepare a pilot pricing proposal and a short-term Dedicated reservation (30–90 days) to validate in your environment (VPC option available).

Are you available Tue/Wed 10–12 PT next week?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
[Attachments: redwood_vs_hyperscaler_abtest_results.csv, p95_p99_latency_plots.pdf, test_configurations.md]
